contract.goal: a removable Kafka-shaped log in the shared PostgreSQL database that the outbox writes to and unmodified @KafkaListener consumers read from, chosen per consumed topic, with a draining cutover
contract.output: new module messaging-db-spring-boot-starter (library, parent common) + one removability ArchUnit rule in architecture-rules + reactor <module> + ludwig-bom entry; README.md/README.ru.md; CHANGELOG entries
constraints: no edit to messaging-spring-boot-starter, outbox-spring-boot-starter, or any service/listener/container-factory bean/outbox route
no DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer declared in the new module
changesets in Liquibase formatted SQL per unify-sql-migrations
do not touch the unrelated uncommitted work already in the tree
done_when: mvn -pl :<each dependent of architecture-rules per scripts/manifest.sh module build/architecture-rules> -am verify

decisions: Spike (group 1) answered by javap against spring-kafka 3.2.4 before writing code, then proven by the real integration tests rather than throwaway spike ITs. Scope note: the spike task names (FactoryWrapSpikeIT etc.) are replaced by the ITs that exercise the same fact; each group-1 task is ticked only when that IT has run green.

RecordInterceptor is not publicly reachable from a container (AbstractMessageListenerContainer.getRecordInterceptor is protected), so the log container composes every RecordInterceptor bean in the context - the same beans ListenerContainerFactoryBuilder composes. Design D2's named fallback.

The consumer name is not on the factory, and the consumer's retry/DLT settings are resolved by it. ListenerContainerFactoryBuilder is therefore proxied (Spring AOP, proxyTargetClass) by the same BeanPostProcessor that replaces the factories, recording factory -> name from forJsonPayload/forTextPayload's first argument. No edit to messaging.

Kafka-read dead letters in ACTIVE mode: the Kafka container's CommonErrorHandler is replaced (container.setCommonErrorHandler is public) by a DefaultErrorHandler built from the same resolved settings, wrapping messaging's AuditingDeadLetterRecoverer around a log-appending delegate. No DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer is declared. The backoff arithmetic (maxAttempts - 1) is duplicated from the builder with a comment tying the two together.

Outbox write path reuses the outbox's own KafkaOutboxDispatcher over a KafkaTemplate whose ProducerFactory returns a MockProducer subclass that appends to the log. Header building therefore stays in exactly one place; nothing in the outbox changes.

Design D4 revised during implementation: one record per claim, not a batch per round. Each poll claims a partition with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on a raw pooled connection (never thread-bound, because JpaTransactionManager refuses to start when a JDBC connection is already bound for its DataSource), handles one record, updates the position and commits. A crash costs one redelivery and no lock is held across more than one listener call. batch-size and round-timeout properties dropped as no longer meaningful.

Schema migration: changesets take pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('ludwig-messaging-db')) and use IF NOT EXISTS instead of a table-exists precondition - that covers both a service whose changelog table never saw the changeset and two services racing. Rollback is '--rollback NOT REQUIRED' on purpose: one service's rollback must not drop the log every other service uses.

MessagingDbProperties is validated in LogStore's constructor (schema identifier pattern, partitions >= 1), not with Bean Validation annotations, so the check holds without a validator on the classpath; jakarta.validation-api not added.

Reversal of the earlier 'no Bean Validation' decision: architecture-rules' configuration-properties-are-validated rule requires @Validated. Rather than disable a rule, MessagingDbProperties is @Validated with @NotNull/@Min/@Pattern, jakarta.validation-api is optional (as in messaging) and spring-boot-starter-validation is test-scoped. LogStore keeps its own schema check because the name is interpolated into SQL.

MessagingDbProperties moved from config to settings: config<->consumer was a package cycle (cycles.modules-are-free-of-cycles). Same resolution messaging uses; architecture-rules.properties widens the configuration role with ..settings..
ludwig.messaging.db.schema is fixed once deployed: Liquibase checksums formatted SQL with the parameter substituted. Documented in the properties javadoc, README and design D6.

Group-1 and 5.1 honesty notes in tasks.md: ordering under contention is proven with three workers of one JVM, not three instances; LogPurgeJob scheduling is not exercised by a test; the missing-group-id refusal has no test.

Scope change (user-approved, 2026-10-21): the starter replaces named clusters (ludwig.messaging.db.clusters, default [internal]) instead of the single kafka transport, and the per-topic consume list is removed - a listener reads one cluster. Depends on the new change add-kafka-clusters, whose KafkaClusterProducers bean becomes the producer seam. Task group 10 added; the contract's goal is unchanged, its 'chosen per consumed topic' wording is superseded by 'chosen per cluster'.

User instruction (2026-10-21): fix the unused java.util.ArrayList import in security-spring-boot-starter AuthorizationDeniedAuditListener. Removed (one line); security-spring-boot-starter checkstyle-validate passes.

User instruction (2026-10-21): remove 'return Collections.emptyList();' and the Collections import from security-spring-boot-starter AuthorizationDeniedAuditListener. Done; the file is now identical to its state before commit 3065ec4 (git diff 3065ec4~1 empty) and compiles.
failures: LogOnlyTransportIT attempt 1: context failed - Boot's own LiquibaseAutoConfiguration looked for db/changelog/db.changelog-master.yaml, which the test application does not have. Fixed in the test with spring.liquibase.enabled=false; module SpringLiquibase beans are unaffected.

LogOnlyTransportIT attempt 2: 3/9 failed - every dead-letter append failed. Cause: kafka_dlt-original-partition is 4 binary bytes, all NUL for partition 0; NUL is valid UTF-8 so it was stored as text, and PostgreSQL jsonb rejects \u0000. Fixed in LogStore.utf8: a value containing NUL is stored as base64. 9/9 green on attempt 3.

MixedTransportIT attempt 1: context failed with Liquibase checksum validation - three test contexts with different ludwig.messaging.db.schema values shared one PostgreSQL and one DATABASECHANGELOG. A real constraint, not a test artefact (see decision on schema). Tests now share the default schema and isolate by topic and group id.
ArchitectureTest attempt 1: 2 failures - config<->consumer package cycle, and @ConfigurationProperties without @Validated. Both fixed in code, no rule disabled for them.

StartupValidationTest attempts 1-2: SimpleKafkaListenerEndpoint does not exist in spring-kafka 3.2.4, then StaticListableBeanFactory's provider rejects getObject(); switched to MethodKafkaListenerEndpoint and DefaultListableBeanFactory.

Gate (task 9): mvn -q validate and 7 of the 11 architecture-rules dependents (crud-service-example, file-action, grpc-client, grpc-server, notification-service, pat, user-settings) stop at security-spring-boot-starter's checkstyle-validate: an unused java.util.ArrayList import in sources/security-spring-boot-starter/.../audit/AuthorizationDeniedAuditListener.java. That file is modified in the working tree by work outside this change and was not touched here, so it was not fixed here. check_image_pins fails on an archived proposal of another change; check_api_baseline fails because nexus.example.internal is unreachable (same environmental failure recorded by unify-sql-migrations).
